topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the cancer biology lecture series and sets out the learning outcomes for this lecture.

topics.label: Accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the stepwise accumulation of cellular changes as a model of cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why normal tissue organisation is essential to understanding cancer and why isolated cell cultures cannot fully represent it.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis as features of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how malignant tumours breach surrounding tissues and spread to distant sites, using clinical and histological comparisons with benign tumours.

topics.label: Progression to malignancy and the risks of benign tumours
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign tumours can progress and why benign status alone does not establish their clinical risk.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Patterns of tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare how frequently different tumour types occur across populations and species.

topics.label: Cancer detection and screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale for detecting cancer early and evaluate how effectively screening achieves that goal in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and revision guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the learning outcomes and directs students towards revision, practicals and the next lecture.
